rejected.title: Climate change and health
card: Climate change is a long-term rise in global temperatures, mostly caused by greenhouse gases from human activity. It affects health in several ways.
Heat and extreme weather
Heatwaves can cause heat stress and death, especially for older people. Floods, fires and storms can injure people and damage homes, water supplies and food crops.
Disease patterns
Warmer and wetter conditions can let disease-carrying mosquitoes live in new areas. Disease risk can then change in places where it was once low.
Unequal effects
Poorer countries tend to be hit hardest. They often have fewer resources to prepare, to rebuild and to run health services, even though they usually add less to the problem.
rejected.remember: Heat, extreme weather and shifting disease can all harm health, and poorer countries tend to suffer most.

a.q: Why do poorer countries tend to be hit hardest by the health effects of climate change?
opts: They often have fewer resources to prepare and rebuild
They often produce most of the world's greenhouse gases
They often face global warming while rich nations do not
They often have older populations more prone to heat stress
a.why: Poorer countries often lack the money and health services to prepare for floods or heatwaves and to rebuild afterwards. The option about producing most greenhouse gases is tempting, but poorer countries usually add less to the problem.
a.clue: Think about what a country needs when a disaster strikes.

b.q: A warming climate lets mosquitoes survive in a highland region where they could not live before. What is the most likely health effect of this change?
opts: Mosquito-borne disease may spread to people there
Heat stress may become the main new risk there
Food crops may fail and cause undernutrition there
Disease risk may stay limited to the lowlands below
b.why: Mosquitoes carry disease, so when they can live in a new area, disease risk can rise where it was once low. Heat stress and crop failure are real effects of climate change, but they do not come from the mosquitoes arriving, which is the change the question asks about.
b.clue: Ask what the mosquitoes themselves bring with them.

a.q: Why do poorer countries tend to be hit hardest by the health effects of climate change?
opts: They have fewer resources to prepare and recover
They produce most of the greenhouse gases globally
They have more extreme weather than any wealthy country
They have no disease-carrying mosquitoes to begin with
a.why: Poorer countries often lack the money and services to prepare for floods or heat and to rebuild afterwards. The option about producing most greenhouse gases is tempting, but poorer countries usually add less to the problem.
a.clue: Think about the ability to prepare and recover, not who caused the problem.

b.q: A warming climate lets mosquitoes survive in a highland region of a country where they could not live before. What is the most likely health effect?
opts: Mosquito-borne disease may appear where risk was once low
Mosquito-borne disease will fall because it is warmer
Heat stress will become the only health risk there
Floods will stop affecting the water supply there
b.why: Warmer and wetter conditions can let mosquitoes live in new areas, so disease risk can change in places where it was once low. The option about disease falling reverses the effect, as warming can help mosquitoes spread.
b.clue: Where mosquitoes can live decides where the diseases they carry can spread.

a.best: They have fewer resources to prepare and recover

b.best: Mosquito-borne disease may appear where risk was once low

The remember line says poorer countries 'are hit hardest', but the card says they 'tend to be hit hardest'. The hedge is dropped.
